Let X be connected and compact, dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, and fix a smooth positive probability volume dV. All potentials are genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, with pole values included. A smooth real (1,1) background theta is big if theta+dd^c rho>=epsilon h for a genuine potential rho, a Hermitian h and epsilon>0; it need not be closed. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C, and equivalence is mutual order. I(tu) uses |g|^2 exp(-tu), with no extra factor 2; ideal equivalence means equality at every real t>0. P_(theta,F)[u] is the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=F with v preceq u; P_(theta,F)[u]_I uses ideal-equivalent competitors. The zero-obstacle operations are P_theta[u] and P_theta[u]_I. An ordinary model is a normalized fixed point p=P_theta[p], and an ideal model also satisfies p=P_theta[p]_I. Extended products are non-pluripolar products with smooth-background corrections. Lower and upper singularity volumes are the infimum and supremum of extended mass over the entire fixed ordinary type, not the raw mass of one representative. BMP means finite supremum v_+(h) over all bounded h-psh potentials, and positive lower mass means the corresponding infimum v_-(h)>0; these are separate properties. Original S06 asks for type-sensitive regularity and stability criteria for equations in arbitrary prescribed ordinary or relative envelope types on smooth big possibly nonclosed backgrounds, beyond resolved logarithmic and exceptional minimal cases. At density zeros, find conditions on density and residual geometry yielding a smooth or Holder residual, and distinguish regularity on the complement from extension across the singular set. The relative envelope class E_env(X,theta,phi) consists of u preceq phi such that for every t>=1 some theta-psh a satisfies t^(-1)a+(1-t^(-1))phi<=u. Envelope equality is not its unrestricted definition. Also address singular envelopes and weighted extremals outside the known uniform density-in-capacity regimes. For a compact non-pluripolar K, continuous obstacle w and selecting potential phi, one precise weighted ideal envelope is the usc supremum of theta-psh a ideal-more-singular than phi with a<=w quasi-everywhere on K. Ideal order means I(ta) subset I(t phi) for every t>0. Declare any different ordinary or weighted version explicitly. Known background: local continuity above a locally bounded strict barrier, local Holder control for minimal Lp solutions, and smoothness on the full regular locus of an analytic strict barrier with smooth positive density are established under their precise hypotheses. Resolved logarithmic positive residuals and specified exceptional minimal types have quantified Holder remainders. Smooth positive global volume forms give ample-locus smoothness in every closed big Kahler class. Smooth density only on a smaller open set can accompany a discontinuous bounded solution. Smooth density zeros and their necessary exceptional vanishing order alone do not imply a smooth Hessian; explicit compact power-blowup and Pogorelov cases are already known. Finite ramification pullback and nonclosed Hopf examples already describe specified smooth zeros and residuals. A smooth positive dual maximizer already forces a smooth exact threshold equation, even at zeros. None of these settles arbitrary prescribed types or all singular extremals. No new regularity criterion, type, geometry or proof is supplied.
